mainEntity.name: How much does a Land Rover Defender 90 D240 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt Land Rover Defender 90 D240 engine typically costs between £4,800 and £7,000 for supply only. Reconditioned units start around £3,500, while used engines can be found from £2,000. Prices vary based on whether you choose supply-only or a full supply and fit service.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Land Rover Defender 90 D240?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early warning signs include a distinct metallic rattling noise from the engine bay during cold starts, which may fade as the oil warms up. You might also experience reduced performance, engine management lights, or rough idling due to incorrect valve timing.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Land Rover Defender 90 D240?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, given the current classic and modern vehicle market. A well-maintained Land Rover Defender 90 D240 holds a value of £22,000 to £35,000+. Investing £4,800-£7,000 in a rebuilt engine with a 12-month warranty is financially viable and protects the appreciating asset value of the vehicle.

mainEntity.name: What is the 204DTD engine code in the Land Rover Defender 90 D240?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 204DTD is the specific 2.0-litre four-cylinder Ingenium diesel engine code fitted to the modern L663 Defender 90 D240 (producing 240PS). It features advanced common-rail injection, a mild-hybrid electrical system (MHEV), and stringent Euro 6d emissions controls.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Land Rover Defender 90 D240 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for a Land Rover Defender 90 D240 typically takes 2 to 3 working days. This includes the removal of the old unit, thorough cleaning of the engine bay, installation of the replacement engine, and comprehensive software calibration.

historyTimeline.intro: As part of the modern L663 generation launched in 2020, the Land Rover Defender 90 D240 brings refined 240PS performance and advanced mild-hybrid technology to the iconic short-wheelbase 4x4, continuing a legendary lineage of robust diesel powertrains.

milestones.description: 200Tdi engine code introduced, 2.5L, 111hp (the original modern Defender diesel, known for mechanical simplicity)
300Tdi engine code introduced, 2.5L, 111hp (improved refinement and reliability, though prone to head gasket issues without steel dowel upgrades)
TD5 (10P/15P) engine code introduced, 2.5L, 122hp (brought electronic fuel injection and improved low-end torque)
244DT (Puma) engine code introduced, 2.4L, 122hp (updated for Euro 4 emissions, featuring a Ford-sourced Duratorq block)
DT224 (Puma) engine code introduced, 2.2L, 122hp (Euro 5 compliance with revised turbo and DPF systems)
204DTD (Ingenium) engine code introduced, 2.0L, 240PS (D240 variant) (modern aluminium architecture, mild-hybrid assistance, and advanced emissions controls)

problems.h4: Timing Chain & Oil Dilution - Why the Land Rover Defender 90 D240 204DTD Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Frequent short trips prevent the engine from reaching optimal temperature, leading to fuel wash and oil dilution during DPF regeneration. This thins the oil, accelerating timing chain tensioner wear and potential chain stretch.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Software update, revised PCV system, and strict oil change intervals (max 10k miles)
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for early-stage symptoms without metallic rattling or chain stretch

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing chain kit, revised tensioners, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The definitive solution for catastrophic chain failure or severe oil dilution damage
